newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: AIB to swap most Dauphin shares for ADRs.
newsitem.headline: AIB to swap most Dauphin shares for ADRs.

text.p: Allied Irish Banks Plc (AIB) said on Tuesday it completed its acquisition of Dauphin Deposit Corp, adding that it would swap 85.4 percent of the U.S. bank's shares for AIB American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).
The rest of Dauphin's shares would be exchanged for cash.
Based on an average ADR price of $46.925, the exchange ratio was set at one ADR per one Dauphin common share.
As a result, AIB would issue 161.1 million new ordinary shares, representing 26.9 million ADRs, the bank said in a statement.
AIB said it would issue 12.1 million fewer shares than it would have issued had its ADR price averaged $40, as it did in January when the deal was announced.
AIB made the estimated $1.36 billion acquisition as part of its strategy to expand in the northeastern U.S, merging Dauphin with its First Maryland Bancorp unit.
Under the deal, Dauphin shareholders could elect to receive cash or stock for their shares.
Dealings in the new AIB ordinary shares were expected to begin on Wednesday on the Dublin, New York and London stock markets, the company said.
AIB's shares in London firmed 2.5p to close at 503.5.
